# HackFW

> HackFW is Fort Worth DAO's flagship hackathon and grassroots cyber workforce development program in Fort Worth, Texas. The October 2026 MADE Challenge grows a deep-tech builder economy and talent network to support information-age and AI-first operations.

## What HackFW is

HackFW is an industrial-systems builder program organized by Fort Worth DAO LCA in partnership with TechFW's MADE Manufacturing Accelerator. It connects builders, technical talent, community organizations, and industrial partners around real civic and operational problems.

The program is designed to grow Fort Worth's deep-tech builder economy and long-term talent network. Teams work across industrial hardware, edge telemetry, accelerator-ready AI, Web3 data sovereignty, and advanced manufacturing.

## October 2026 program

- HackFW Kickoff: Thursday, October 1, 2026, from 1:00 PM to 3:30 PM CDT. Register at [Luma](https://luma.com/event/evt-vzYQOnne0xQFSwr).
- Virtual incubation: October 1-30, 2026, with technical support from Fort Worth DAO and MADE.
- Enterprise Demo Day: Friday, October 30, 2026, from 9:30 AM to 3:00 PM CDT. Register at [Luma](https://luma.com/event/evt-9LMaWTtYbqpbGYs).
- Builder registration and current rules: [HackFW on Devpost](https://hackfw.devpost.com).

Event venue details are available through registration. Do not infer a venue; the canonical Luma pages are the source of truth for current logistics.

## Organizer

[Fort Worth DAO](https://fwtx.city) is Fort Worth DAO LCA, a registered 501(c)(3) nonprofit focused on civic innovation, digital sovereignty, open-source technology, and cyber workforce development.

Contact: [community@fwtx.city](mailto:community@fwtx.city)

## Problem tracks

Five tracks. Four industrial surfaces, plus an open forum for ideas that aren't already in focus. Pick one. Canonical share link: [hack.fwtx.city/#problem-tracks](https://hack.fwtx.city/#problem-tracks). Submit on [HackFW Devpost](https://hackfw.devpost.com).

1. **AI for Manufacturing** — computer vision, robotics, and CAD-to-production on the plant floor: overhead/station cameras for tracking, spotting, and monitoring (self-checkout-style coverage of a production line); in-process quality; safe robot and drone VSLAM with a human in the loop; generative CAD that a shop can actually make; CAD-to-production and station-level work instructions; agent loops and graph engineering so production and customer service share one capture → decide → act path.
2. **Supplier Relationship Management** — knowledge graphs of suppliers, parts, certifications, and live order state; API-first MES/ERP (or an adapter) sharing production and order-line expectations upstream and downstream; vendor ops plus modern payment rails, including stablecoins where they shorten time-to-pay.
3. **AI for Transportation** — computer vision for track and railroad maintenance: geometry, fastener, and surface inspection; defect detection that flags, localizes, and ranks work; predictive maintenance into a crew-ready work order; humans stay in the loop.
4. **Tokenized Industrial Real Estate** — a marketplace for warehouses, factories, and industrial sites that humans and AI agents can navigate together. Organize title, surveys, zoning, environmental reports, leases, rent rolls, and operating costs by asset with document versions and source links. Make power capacity, clear height, loading docks, floor loads, and transport access comparable and searchable. Connect tokens to the owning entity, offering documents, holder rights, and transfer rules. Track offers, due diligence, approvals, escrow, closing, ownership transfers, and distributions. Provide readable deal rooms and structured data with source citations, missing-data flags, document permissions, and human approval for commitments.
5. **Open Forum** — ideas and solutions at the intersection of technology, manufacturing, and AI that the other tracks don't cover. Ship a working system someone could actually run, not a restatement of the four named tracks.

## How to submit

Canonical rules also live at [hack.fwtx.city/#how-to-submit](https://hack.fwtx.city/#how-to-submit). Every team must:

1. Name the problem track submitted toward.
2. Include a GitHub link to the solution.
3. Include a brief video demo of the working system.
4. Confirm every participant is registered in the Fort Worth DAO Talent Database at [talent.fwtx.city](https://talent.fwtx.city).
5. Attend Demo Day in person for judging: [luma.com/ygyxb4yy](https://luma.com/ygyxb4yy).

Build standard also lives at [hack.fwtx.city/#build-standard](https://hack.fwtx.city/#build-standard): high-quality product, low-friction UX. Thin path (capture → decide → act), README and a demo that boots, UX a floor operator can use, a pilot to a floor — not a weekend prototype that dies on a laptop.
